key_insight: Clinician LLM use is dominated by documentation and knowledge-retrieval tasks, but public benchmarks largely test different work, so benchmark scores may not predict real clinical deployment.
clinical_relevance: For health systems adopting LLM assistants, evaluation should reflect actual clinician workflows rather than exam-style or curated-case benchmarks alone.
method: Analyzed 127,833 real queries from 6,342 clinicians across 35 specialties during an 8-month rollout.
Classified each query with RCQ-Map, a clinician-validated framework covering task, intent, answerability, missing information, and potential harm.
Compared real-world query mix against 58 public benchmarks from major evaluation suites and frontier model reports.
evidence_signal: Real use was mainly documentation/administration (36.2%) and knowledge retrieval (28.9%), while the median benchmark had no documentation requests and matched only 31% of the real task mix.
watch_item: Benchmark alignment may still miss local workflow differences, and many real queries were not fully answerable as posed, so deployment needs ongoing monitoring beyond offline scores.
paper_title: Clinician use of language models diverges from how the models are evaluated
